part.text:
The implementation is complete. I wrote the solution in the two files:

**`phone_number.h`** — declares a `phone_number` class in the `phone_number` namespace with an explicit constructor taking the raw input string and a `number()` method returning the cleaned 10-digit string.

**`phone_number.cpp`** — the constructor:
1. Scans the input, keeping digits, skipping a leading `+`, and throwing `std::domain_error` on any other character (catches letters and punctuation like `@:!`).
2. If 11 digits remain, the first must be `1` (the only valid NANP country code); it is then stripped. Otherwise 11 digits throws.
3. Anything that isn't exactly 10 digits throws (covers the 9-digit case).
4. The area code (digit 0) and exchange code (digit 3) must be `2`–`9`; otherwise throws.

This handles all the test cases: cleaning punctuation/spaces, `+1` country codes, and all the invalid-length, invalid-character, and invalid area/exchange code rejections (including the 11-digit variants).

One caveat: I attempted to build and run the test suite, but the shell permission system denied every build command (`cmake`, `g++`, `clang++`, `cc` with compile flags), so I couldn't execute `phone_number_test` to verify. The code follows the standard solution for this exercise and should compile cleanly under the CMake setup's `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror` flags. If you can approve the build commands, I can run the tests to confirm.
